subject.title: fix(plugins): preserve already-loaded plugins across scoped harness activation

question: Should harness activation preserve the existing registry through reuse or composition, or is rebuilding every currently live plugin an intentional supported lifecycle?
rationale: The current patch chooses broad plugin re-execution and activation based on historical live state; repository policy instead treats the mutable global registry as compatibility scaffolding and prefers explicit activation planning or request-scoped handles, so an owner must confirm the permitted lifecycle and security boundary.

options.title: Compose without re-registering
options.body: Preserve existing registry registrations and load only missing harness-owned plugins through a lifecycle-owned composition or request-scoped handle.

options.title: Rebuild with full contracts
options.body: Keep the widening approach only after proving plugin registration is safely repeatable, applying the complete activation policy, and covering cleanup and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Pause for registry refactor
options.body: Hold this PR and address the global replacement model in a broader canonical registry-lifecycle change.

recommendation.title: Compose without re-registering
recommendation.body: Preserve existing registry registrations and load only missing harness-owned plugins through a lifecycle-owned composition or request-scoped handle.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the scoped provider-owner harness-loading path and are the strongest history-backed owner for selecting its preservation semantics.
